name: Rhinoplasty tip-narrowing sutures
lead: Tip-narrowing sutures are stitches placed in the lower lateral cartilages of the nose during rhinoplasty to reshape and narrow a broad or bulbous tip without removing cartilage. For people who want a more defined, refined nose tip, the technique offers a way to slim the tip and sharpen its contours from within, rather than by cutting cartilage away. General rhinoplasty references describe sutures as a way to narrow a wide tip by tightening the folded cartilage apex [1].

Reviews describe suture techniques as remodelling the tip by changing the configuration of the tip cartilages and their supporting structures while preserving anatomy and limiting resection; effects are visible during surgery and can be adjusted or reversed, and one review concludes that sutures should be considered instead of tissue excision whenever possible [2]. A 2016 overview of the broad, bulbous tip says earlier reductive techniques produced unnatural results over time, and presents suturing and structural grafting as the contemporary approach [3].

The named sutures in a modern surgeon's repertoire include the medial crural, middle crural, interdomal, transdomal, lateral crural, medial crural anchor, tip rotation, medial crural footplate and lateral crural convexity control sutures [4]. Published work is mostly review articles and surgeon technique descriptions; no randomised trial of tip sutures alone was found.

angle.text: Surgeons use tip sutures to slim a broad tip and improve its contours, often with grafts such as a columellar strut. People seeking a more defined nose tip pursue it as part of rhinoplasty.

infobox: Primary and revision rhinoplasty (open or closed approach)
Refine a wide or bulbous nasal tip

paras: Surgeons can narrow the tip by suturing the cartilage rather than resecting it, and open rhinoplasty is described as giving better visualization and precision for tip work [1]. Suture work is often combined with grafts such as the columellar strut. A video-based review of tip shaping emphasises that nasal tip anatomy has a large effect on the overall look of the nose and focuses on tip sutures and cartilage grafts in open rhinoplasty [5]. Techniques have also been adapted to closed rhinoplasty, for example a septocolumellar loop suture between the medial crura and caudal septum [6].

Suture techniques for reshaping the tip have been used for many decades, with the last two decades before 2003 the most influential in shaping current methods. Early tip techniques sacrificed the integrity of the lateral crus to gain projection, which could disrupt tip support and lead to supratip fullness, asymmetry, tip drop or an overoperated look. Modern tip surgery is built on using sutures to directly reshape and reposition tip components rather than merely secure excised cartilage [4].

A review of tip sutures notes they are powerful enough that they must be performed precisely to avoid creating cosmetic as well as functional problems [7]. Risks are those of rhinoplasty in general; revision surgery accounts for roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations, with pinched or asymmetric tips among reasons cited [1].

No studies found for tip-narrowing sutures alone. Registered trials of related tip surgery include a study of lateral crural steal with a columellar strut (NCT07317947, 22 participants, recruiting) [8] and a comparison of septal advancement flap and columellar strut effect on the tip (NCT06370455, 30 participants, completed) [9]. A 2025 report examined long-term outcomes of primary rhinoplasty more broadly [10].

card.summary: Stitches that reshape the cartilage of a wide nasal tip during rhinoplasty; sources found here are sparse.
card.note: Little dedicated research found; part of rhinoplasty with its general risks.

quick.overview:
Tip-narrowing sutures are stitches placed in the nose cartilage during rhinoplasty to refine a broad or bulbous tip without removing tissue.

Very little dedicated research on the technique alone was found.
quick.mechanism: The stitches pull and hold the tip cartilages in a narrower shape.
quick.risks: Risks are those of rhinoplasty generally, including revision surgery in roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations. It is a surgical procedure.
